name: Salary Per Day Calculator
short: Daily and hourly rate from a monthly salary.
formula: Per-day salary = Monthly salary ÷ Days in the basis (calendar days, 26, 30 or your own).
example: ₹26,000 on a 26-day basis = ₹1,000 per day; 20 paid days = ₹20,000.

faqs.a: Use what your appointment letter or policy says. Calendar days is common; many factories use 26.
On the calendar basis, yes. On a 26-day basis, weekly offs are excluded.

name: Attendance Calculator
short: Attendance percentage and days needed to reach a target.
formula: Attendance % = (Present days + Half days × 0.5) ÷ Working days × 100.

name: Overtime Calculator
short: Overtime pay from salary, hours and rate.
formula: Hourly rate = Monthly salary ÷ Days ÷ Hours per day. OT pay = Hourly rate × Multiplier × OT hours.

faqs.a: The Factories Act sets twice the ordinary rate for covered workers. Check what applies to you.

name: Leave Calculator
short: Leave accrued, available, carried forward and lapsed.
formula: Available = Opening + (Per month × Months) − Taken. Carry forward is limited by your cap.

faqs.a: Leave above the carry-forward cap that is not carried into the next year.

name: Salary Breakup Calculator
short: Split an annual CTC into Basic, HRA and allowances.
formula: Basic = CTC × Basic %. HRA = Basic × HRA %. Employer PF = 12% of Basic (capped at ₹15,000). Special allowance = balance.
example: ₹6,00,000 CTC at 50% basic: Basic ₹25,000, HRA ₹10,000, employer PF ₹1,800.

faqs.q: Is this the only way to structure salary?
faqs.a: No. It is a common split. PayroleHR lets you define any columns you like.

name: Working Days Calculator
formula: Working days = Total days − Weekly offs − Holidays.
example: November 2026 with Sundays off and 2 holidays = 23 working days.

faqs.q: Can I have two weekly offs?
faqs.a: Yes, tick every weekly off day.

name: CTC to In-Hand Calculator
short: Estimate take-home pay from CTC under the new tax regime.
formula: In-hand = Gross − Employee PF − ESI − Professional tax − Monthly TDS (new regime, ₹75,000 standard deduction, 4% cess).
example: ₹12,00,000 CTC at 50% basic: income tax is nil under the new regime (up to about ₹12.75 lakh gross).

faqs.q: Why might my real figure differ?
faqs.a: Bonuses, reimbursements, state professional tax and the old regime all change the result.

name: Gratuity Calculator
short: Gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act.
formula: Gratuity = 15 ÷ 26 × Last Basic + DA × Completed years (more than 6 months counts as a year), capped at ₹20 lakh.

faqs.a: Normally after 5 years of continuous service, or earlier on death or disablement.

name: Payroll Cost Calculator
short: Monthly and annual employer cost for your team.
formula: Cost per employee = Gross + Employer PF + Employer ESI. Total = Cost × Headcount + other costs.
example: 50 staff at ₹20,000 gross / ₹10,000 basic ≈ ₹10.9 lakh a month.

faqs.a: No. Add any provision under other monthly costs.

name: 8th Pay Commission Salary Calculator
short: Estimate your revised salary under the 8th Pay Commission using your current pay level and expected fitment factor. Covers Basic Pay, HRA, and gross salary comparison.
formula: New Basic Pay = Current Basic Pay × Fitment Factor.
example: Pay Level 7, ₹44,900 basic, fitment 2.28x: New Basic ₹1,02,372; Estimated New Gross ₹1,38,220.

faqs.q: What is the expected fitment factor for the 8th Pay Commission?
faqs.a: Most staff associations and economic projections suggest a fitment factor between 1.92x and 2.86x, with 2.28x being widely referenced. The 7th CPC used 2.57x.

faqs.q: Will Dearness Allowance (DA) reset to 0% after 8th CPC implementation?
faqs.a: Yes. Following past pay commissions, accumulated DA (currently 53% as of Jan 2026) is merged into the revised basic pay, and DA resets to 0% on the date of implementation.

faqs.q: How will HRA be calculated under the 8th Pay Commission?
faqs.a: House Rent Allowance (HRA) will be calculated on the new revised basic pay at standard classification rates (27% for X class metro cities, 18% for Y class, and 9% for Z class).

faqs.q: Who is covered under the 8th Central Pay Commission?
faqs.a: The 8th CPC covers approximately 50 lakh Central Government employees (including defence personnel and railway staff) and nearly 65 lakh pensioners across India.
